title: Status of Invasive Species in B.C.
summary: Explore current aquatic invasive-species occurrence records summarized across B.C.'s 36 ecological drainage units, with a dedicated freshwater-fish view.
sourceNote: The original Environmental Reporting BC page was published in 2015. This project reruns its ecological-drainage-unit aggregation against the current public Aquatic Invasive Species service. Forty source polygons are grouped into one reusable set of 36 named drainage-unit boundaries; 122 coastal or edge records are assigned to the nearest unit, following the repository's nearest-unit method. The invasive-alien-plant-site map is not republished because its source is Access Only and the repository depends on a non-public supplementary label file.
details: Click or tap a drainage unit for the number of distinct aquatic invasive species and occurrence records in the current service.
Switch to the fish view to see the distribution of known invasive freshwater fish species and read each unit's species list.
Occurrence data document detections; absence of a mapped record does not establish that an invasive species is absent.

scenes.label: Aquatic species
scenes.title: Aquatic invasive species are recorded across most southern drainage units
scenes.text: The current service contains 8,490 point records. This view counts distinct species within each ecological drainage unit rather than drawing thousands of overlapping occurrence markers.

callout.label: Mapped records
callout.detail: Fish, plants, amphibians, reptiles, algae, and invertebrates.

scenes.label: Freshwater fish
scenes.title: Invasive freshwater fish occur in two thirds of drainage units
scenes.text: Twenty-four of the 36 named units contain at least one mapped invasive fish species in the current service. Select a unit to see its species list.

callout.label: Units with fish records
callout.detail: Occurrence records are unevenly distributed and reflect monitoring effort.

scenes.label: Lower Fraser
scenes.title: Lower Fraser has the largest mapped invasive-species count
scenes.text: The Lower Fraser drainage unit contains 96 distinct aquatic invasive species in the current source, including 20 invasive fish species.
